title: Compact-support comparison with completed and condensed coefficient realization
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of positive prime characteristic $p$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Fix a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{g}Y)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For $n\geq1$ and $T=X,\overline X,Y$, set $A_{n,T}=(R/t^n)_T$, $\widehat R_T=\lim_n A_{n,T}$, and let $\mathcal I_T(R)$ be the completed integral category of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. Use the strict reduction functor $\mathcal R_T$, the semilinear system category $\mathscr S_T$, and $\mathcal L_T=R\lim U_T$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Let $F_n=Rg_{*,n}j_!$. Let $\mathcal F$ denote its functor on normalized coefficient systems, with the canonical projection comparisons. Define
$$P_RK=R\lim\mathcal T_f^c(K),$$
where $\mathcal T_f^c$ is the actual strict compact-support reduction-tower functor of [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor], with its semilinear lift given by the geometric models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

Then $P_R$ is an exact $R$-linear functor $\mathcal I_X(R)\to\mathcal I_Y(R)$. There is a specified natural isomorphism of normalized derived semilinear systems
$$\alpha_K:\mathcal R_Y(P_RK)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F(\mathcal R_XK).$$
Its evaluation is the canonical map $(P_RK)\otimes^L_{\widehat R_Y}A_{n,Y}\to F_n(K\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}A_{n,X})$ induced by the total-limit projections. In particular this comparison includes transitions and all coefficient coherences, rather than only its evaluations.

Let $J_T:\mathcal I_T(R)[1/t]\simeq\mathcal C_E^c(T)$ be the derived coefficient-extension equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization]. For the coefficient ring $E_{\overline X}^c$, let $j_{!,E}$ be sheafification of the extension-by-zero module presheaf on the open slice site, applied termwise to complexes [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Let $Rg_{*,E}$ be the derived direct image with the coefficient action and pullback identification of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. Put $P_E^c=Rg_{*,E}j_{!,E}$ on those condensed module-object categories, and use the identical composite to define $P_\Omega^c$ for the finite-extension-valued coefficient ring $\Omega_T^c$ of [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit], $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. These composites preserve the indicated bounded constructible categories. There is a natural isomorphism
$$a_{f,E,K}:J_Y((P_RK)[1/t])\xrightarrow{\sim}P_E^cJ_X(K[1/t]).$$
For finite $E\subset F\subset\Omega$ and also for $F=\Omega$, put $T_{E,F}^T=F_T^c\otimes^L_{E_T^c}-$ (with $F_T^c=\Omega_T^c$ in the latter case). The canonical coefficient projection comparison is an isomorphism
$$T_{E,F}^YP_E^c\xrightarrow{\sim}P_F^cT_{E,F}^X.$$
For finite $F/E$, write $K_S$ for completed integral scalar extension to $S=\mathcal O_F$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. There is a canonical comparison $(P_RK)_S\simeq P_SK_S$, compatible with $\alpha$, $a$, and the preceding condensed projection comparison after rationalization. All these specified comparisons preserve morphisms, shifts, identities, towers of finite coefficient extensions and compactification-refinement maps, with their composition coherences. This is a comparison of compact-support functors only; it makes no assertion about their right adjoints.

proof.text: Write $B_T=\widehat R_T$ and $P_R^0=Rg_{*,R}j_{!,R}$. Finite type over $k$ gives noetherianity and finite dimension; $\overline X$ is also finite type since $g$ is proper. Thus $j$ is quasi-compact, all three schemes are noetherian of finite dimension, and $\ell$ is invertible. The quotients $R/t^n$ are finite and perfect over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect], so they meet the adic hypotheses used below. The coefficient inverse-image identifications commute with every quotient. Apply [lem-cbc-integral-compact-support-uniform-restriction] to $c$: it gives an exact $R$-linear $P_R^0:\mathcal I_X(R)\to\mathcal I_Y(R)$. Apply it also to $j$, compactified by $j$ followed by the proper identity of $\overline X$. Hence $j_{!,R}K\in\mathcal I_{\overline X}(R)$ and is complete. Here $j_!$ is exact sheafified open extension and proper image is derived separately.

source.place: 6.7.2, 6.7.6–6.7.8; agent assembly of the cited ordinary-derived statements

proof.text:
Put $N_K=\mathcal F(\mathcal R_XK)$. On the ordinary derived ringed diagram sites of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], form the proper coefficient counit transpose followed by the open scalar comparison. This gives the system map $b_K:\mathcal R_Y(P_R^0K)\to N_K$, with evaluation
$$ (Rg_{*,R}j_{!,R}K)\otimes^L_{B_Y}A_{n,Y}\longrightarrow Rg_{*,n}((j_{!,R}K)\otimes^L_{B_{\overline X}}A_{n,\overline X})\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_{*,n}j_{!,n}K_n.$$
The first map is the diagram-site projection isomorphism of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits], including all quotient transitions; its complete input was checked in Step 1. The second is [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], applied to the identity on schemes with ring change $B\to A_n$, also on the ringed diagram sites. Its statement already supplies the derived comparison, so no K-flat preservation lemma is proved inline here. [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] supplies the indicated proper-image coefficient restriction. Evaluation detects isomorphisms by the ordinary-system theorem, so $b_K$ is invertible. The normalization isomorphisms and their quotient cocycle for $\mathcal R_Y(P_R^0K)$ are expressly given in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Transporting those transition adjoints along $b_K$ proves $N_K$ normalized. No internal Hom, flatness of reduction maps, or inference of equality from evaluations is used.

source.place: 6.7.2 and 6.7.16–6.7.17; agent assembly of the cited ordinary-derived statements

proof.text:
The strict tower underlying $N_K$ is $\mathcal T_f^c(K)$: use its defining lift, reduction followed by exact open extension, separately derived proper image, and coefficient restriction. The ordinary-system operations and the coefficient-restriction comparisons identify these same composites as derived strict-diagram functors [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections, lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison]. This identifies constructions, rather than arbitrary towers with the same evaluations. Thus $P_RK=\mathcal L_YN_K$. With unit $u$ and counit $e$ of $\mathcal R_Y\dashv\mathcal L_Y$, set
$$q_K=\mathcal L_Y(b_K)u_{P_R^0K}:P_R^0K\longrightarrow P_RK.$$
The unit is invertible by completeness in Step 1 and the completion-unit clause of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Put $\alpha_K=e_{N_K}$. Naturality of $e$ and the adjunction triangle identity give $\alpha_K\mathcal R_Y(q_K)=b_K$; hence $\alpha_K$ is invertible. The evaluation-calculus statement identifies its evaluations with the scalar adjuncts of the actual limit projections, as required. Exactness follows from the exact strict tower and exact total-limit functors. Their scalar action is the termwise constant $R$-action, so the composite is $R$-linear. Its output is in $\mathcal I_Y(R)$ by $q_K$ and Step 1.

source.place: 6.7.6–6.7.7; agent assembly of the cited ordinary-derived statements

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] to the identity on $\overline X$ with coefficient change $B_{\overline X}\to E_{\overline X}^c$. Its specified open-unit adjunct gives
$$E_{\overline X}^c\otimes^L_{B_{\overline X}}j_{!,R}K\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,E}(E_X^c\otimes^L_{B_X}K).$$
The pullback coefficient maps are those of Step 1 and of the condensed coefficient category. The underlying map on the open is the identity under balanced tensor identifications. Localize $j_{!,R}$ and this comparison by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]; preservation of $\mathcal I$ was proved in Step 1. Since $J$ is precisely derived coefficient extension, this is $J_{\overline X}(j_{!,R}K[1/t])\cong j_{!,E}J_X(K[1/t])$. Essential surjectivity of $J_X$ then proves that $j_{!,E}$ preserves $\mathcal C_E^c$.

source.place: 6.8.14–6.8.15 and 6.7.6; agent assembly of the cited ordinary-derived statements

proof.text:
Define $a_{f,E,K}$ by the ordered composite
$$J_Y(P_RK[1/t])\xrightarrow{J_Y(q_K^{-1}[1/t])}J_Y((Rg_{*,R}j_{!,R}K)[1/t])\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_{*,E}J_{\overline X}(j_{!,R}K[1/t])\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_{*,E}j_{!,E}J_X(K[1/t]).$$
The middle comparison, including its counits, is the direct-image clause of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization] for $g$; the last is Step 4. Its source belongs to $\mathcal C_E^c(Y)$ by Step 3. Every input is realized from a lattice, so the actual ambient composite $P_E^c$ preserves the claimed category. This also fixes the normalization of $a$ on morphisms.

source.place: 6.8.14–6.8.15; agent assembly of the cited ordinary-derived statements

proof.text: For finite $E\subset F$, [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-flat-coefficient-calculus] says that $F_T^c$ is finite free over $E_T^c$. Their inverse-image identifications are the coefficient-category composition identifications. Apply [lem-sp-finite-free-direct-image-coherence] to $g$: its specified counit transpose is the proper coefficient isomorphism. Follow it by the normalized open scalar isomorphism of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. The result is exactly the canonical $T_{E,F}^YP_E^c\xrightarrow{\sim}P_F^cT_{E,F}^X$. The finite-direct-sum invertibility argument is an input theorem here, rather than an inline lemma.

source.place: 6.7.14 and 6.8.15; agent assembly of the cited ordinary-derived statements

proof.text: For $S=\mathcal O_F$ put $C_T=-\otimes^L_{B_T}\widehat S_T$. Its identification $\chi_T:C_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}K_S$ is the specified quotient-augmentation map of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]; that statement also supplies finite freeness and completeness of $C_TK$. It preserves $\mathcal I_T$: on a stratum with model $B_T\otimes_R^LP$, scalar extension has model $\widehat S_T\otimes_S^L(S\otimes_R^LP)$, and a bounded finite projective model stays such after scalar extension. Apply the stratified-perfect characterization, which includes the required witnesses. The coefficient inverse-image identifications for $S$ are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Apply [lem-sp-finite-free-direct-image-coherence] to $B\to\widehat S$ and $g$, then [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] to $j$. This gives a specified isomorphism $d_{S/R}:C_YP_R^0\xrightarrow{\sim}P_S^0C_X$. Conjugate it by the $q$ of Step 3 and the $\chi_T$ to obtain $(P_RK)_S\xrightarrow{\sim}P_SK_S$. This does not assume that $R/t^n\to S/v^n$ is flat.

source.place: 6.7.16–6.7.17 and 6.8.15; agent assembly of the cited ordinary-derived statements

proof.text:
Account for ramification before comparing reductions. The coefficient maps in [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] put $t$ in the maximal ideal of $S$. Write $t=uv^e$ in this DVR, with $u$ a unit and $e\geq1$, using [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Thus $(t^n)S=(v^{en})$. The canonical quotient isomorphisms in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], applied to $S$ at exponent $en$ and to $R$ at exponent $n$, give
$$\widehat S_T/t^n\widehat S_T\cong(S/v^{en})_T=:D_{n,T},\qquad B_T/t^nB_T\cong A_{n,T}.$$
Reducing the finite free $B_T$-module $\widehat S_T$ from [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] gives $D_{n,T}\cong A_{n,T}^{\oplus[F:E]}$ as modules. Balanced derived scalar associativity [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] identifies $(C_TK)\otimes^L_{\widehat S_T}D_{n,T}$ with $K_n\otimes^L_{A_{n,T}}D_{n,T}$. All maps here are the stated quotient maps; equal ideals do not identify $S/v^n$ with $S/t^n$.

source.place: 6.7.16–6.7.17; ramified quotient bookkeeping; agent assembly of the cited ordinary-derived statements

proof.text:
The coefficient cocycles are now applications of cited identities. For finite $E\subset F\subset H$, the proper projection comparisons satisfy the transitivity equation of [lem-sp-finite-free-direct-image-coherence]; the same equation without a freeness assumption is [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle]. Apply the latter also to completed rings. The open comparison is its open-unit adjunct from [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]; balanced associativity and mate pasting give its successive-extension comparison. Therefore, with tensor associators inserted,
$$d_{H/E}=P_H^0(\tau_X)\,d_{H/F}\,C_{H/F}(d_{F/E})\,\tau_Y^{-1},$$
and the identical equation holds for finite condensed coefficient comparisons. Identity extensions give identity maps. These are equations in the appropriate coefficient derived categories, not equations inferred after forgetting coefficients.

source.place: 6.7.16–6.7.17 and 6.8.15; coefficient cocycles; agent assembly of the cited ordinary-derived statements

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle] on the ordinary ringed diagram sites to the commuting coefficient square whose two paths are
$$\Delta B_T\longrightarrow\Delta\widehat S_T\longrightarrow D_{\bullet,T},\qquad\Delta B_T\longrightarrow A_{\bullet,T}\longrightarrow D_{\bullet,T}.$$
Both routes are the homomorphism $B_T\to D_{n,T}$ at each level, as a strict ring-system equality. Thus the proper comparison for coefficient extension followed by reduction equals reduction followed by coefficient extension. The open factors have the same equation by their open-unit normalization and mate pasting. This is precisely the square between the $b_R,b_S$ of Step 2 (the latter restricted to levels $en$) and $d_{S/R}$ of Step 7 under Step 8's balanced identifications. Its equality holds on $D(\mathscr S(D_\bullet))$, using [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], before applying the forgetful functor. It includes quotient transitions; no assertion that evaluated arrows detect equality is used.

source.place: 6.7.16–6.7.17; coherent reduction square; agent assembly of the cited ordinary-derived statements

proof.text: To pass that square to limits, use [lem-sp-strict-tower-arithmetic-restriction] on $\widehat S$-module towers: restriction $m=en$ preserves the canonical derived limit, its projections and strict augmentation maps. For scalar extension $C_T$, [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] supplies exact countable products in both module categories. Finite freeness makes $C_T$ exact and its canonical product comparison invertible: in a finite basis it is the identity between the same finite copies of a product. Hence [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] gives its specified limit comparison, preserving augmentations. The map $\chi$ of Step 7 is exactly that quotient augmentation. Apply these functorial comparisons to Step 10's strict-system square and use the natural reduction-limit unit. The result is the commuting square for $q_R,q_S$ and $d_{S/R}$, hence for $\alpha$ by $\alpha\mathcal R(q)=b$. For the full $S/v^m$ tower use its quotient map from any $S/v^{en}$ with $en\geq m$; the cocycle of Step 10 identifies these maps independently of the choice. Successive restrictions and units agree by the same arithmetic-restriction theorem and coefficient cocycle. This gives the asserted integral scalar coherences including all reductions.

source.place: 6.7.16–6.7.17; normalized total-limit passage; agent assembly of the cited ordinary-derived statements

proof.text: For the mixed square with $a$, the ring square $B_T\to\widehat S_T$, $B_T\to E_T^c$, $\widehat S_T\to F_T^c$, $E_T^c\to F_T^c$ commutes by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations]. Apply [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle] to it. The proper comparison in $J$ preserves the adjunction counit by [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization], so its proper factors are exactly these coefficient transposes; the open factors are the normalized comparisons of Step 4. Step 11 gives the $q$ square. Substituting these three squares in the displayed definition of $a$ in Step 5 gives compatibility of the integral comparison after rationalization with $a$ and with the condensed coefficient comparison. Localization preserves the equalities by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]. This argument uses the entire commuting ring square, including ramified reductions through Step 11.

source.place: 6.8.14–6.8.15; mixed realization square; agent assembly of the cited ordinary-derived statements

proof.text: For $E\subset\Omega$ use the small filtered poset of finite $H\subset\Omega$ containing $E$. It is final in all finite intermediate fields by taking composita. For $L\in\mathcal C_E^c(X)$, [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-coefficient-complex-presentation] gives simultaneous coefficient complexes and their actual cocone maps. Choose a lower cohomological bound $a$ for $L$. Exact finite and $\Omega$ scalar extension and exact $j_!$ keep that bound. Open extension commutes with the coefficient colimit since it is a left adjoint. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity] to $g$, which is proper and hence qcqs, in the $E^c$-module category. Coefficient restriction commutes with proper image and reflects isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. Thus the colimit of Step 6's isomorphisms gives an isomorphism $T_{E,\Omega}^YP_E^cL\to P_\Omega^cT_{E,\Omega}^XL$. The presentation theorem identifies the cocone maps under coefficient transposition, so this is the canonical projection map. Throughout $\Omega^c$ is the finite-subfield-valued coefficient ring, and only bounded-below continuity has been applied.

source.place: 6.8.14(1) and 6.8.15; agent assembly of the cited ordinary-derived statements

proof.text: Every $\mathcal C_\Omega^c(X)$ object is $T_{E,\Omega}^XL$ by [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit]. Step 13 identifies its image under the actual ambient composite with $T_{E,\Omega}^YP_E^cL$, which belongs to $\mathcal C_\Omega^c(Y)$ by the scalar-preservation clause and Step 5. The coefficient cocycle with target $\Omega$ is the arbitrary-ring cocycle of Step 9, so direct and successive coefficient maps agree. For arbitrary morphisms choose a common finite field using the two-colimit's morphism clause. Naturality there gives naturality of the result; independence follows because two finite representatives agree after further extension, again by that node. This also preserves identities.

source.place: 6.8.14(1) and 6.8.15; descent of transformations; agent assembly of the cited ordinary-derived statements

proof.text: For a proper refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$, use the intrinsic clopen-section mate of [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting]. It defines the actual map between the semilinear compact-support systems, has identity and successive-refinement laws before evaluation, and restricts to the specified constant-$R$ tower map. Its finite inputs have bounded-below etale-origin witnesses by membership in $\mathcal I_X(R)$, so [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] gives invertibility there. Joint conservativity of ordinary system evaluation gives invertibility on systems. Apply [lem-pur-ringed-refinement-coefficient-square] to $\Delta B\to A_\bullet$, then apply $Rg_{2,*}$. Identify $Rg_{1,*}=Rg_{2,*}Ru_*$ using the adjunction-compatible composition of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. The coefficient cocycle and [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identify the pasted coefficient transpose, giving the refinement square for $b$ with its clopen normalization. The constant/completed comparison identifies the limit units. Taking total limit and using naturality of the unit in Step 3 gives the refinement square for $q$. Naturality of the reduction-limit counit gives it for $\alpha$. All equalities are obtained from ordinary derived-system transformations.

source.place: 6.7.6–6.7.7; integral refinement square; agent assembly of the cited ordinary-derived statements

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-ringed-refinement-coefficient-square] to $B\to\widehat S$, $B\to E^c$ and $E^c\to F^c$. These coefficient sheaves have exactly the inverse-image identifications already checked. It gives the refinement squares for the proper/open composites, with the same clopen projection and counit transpose used in Steps 5–7. Combine them with Step 15's $q$ square and the counit-preserving $J$ comparison. This gives refinement compatibility for completed integral scalar extension and for $a$ and finite condensed scalar extension. Rationalization preserves these equations. Step 13 takes their finite-stage cocone maps to the same equation at $\Omega$, and Step 14 removes the finite presentation choice. Successive-refinement laws are inherited from the strict-system pasting theorem; the coefficient cocycles of Steps 9–12 give compatibility with towers of extensions.

source.place: 6.7.7 and 6.8.15; field refinement square; agent assembly of the cited ordinary-derived statements

proof.text: Finally all constructions respect the canonical shifts. Derived pullback/direct-image units and counits do so by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift], and coefficient projection does so by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] and [lem-sp-finite-free-direct-image-coherence]. Exact open extension acts degreewise, and its normalized open-unit and clopen identity/zero maps shift to those same maps. The new coefficient and refinement statements include their shift equations. Total limit is exact; its projection-normalized units and comparisons come from ordinary derived adjunctions on the ringed diagram topoi. Rationalization and the bounded-below coefficient-colimit comparisons preserve their shift structures. Therefore the comparisons constructed above are natural exact-functor comparisons with the asserted shifts, identities, coefficient towers and refinement coherences. No exceptional right adjoint or enhanced category has been introduced.
